text:
marta: quick decision needed for the notification preview UI. two options from the prototype tests: collapse suppressed channels (clean list) or show them greyed with a badge. testers were split.

nina: collapsed list looks tidy but people assumed channels were accidentally removed. one tester clicked config and couldn't find the missing channel.

sam: collapsed simplifies visual noise. implementation would be easy: filter suppressed channels out of the preview list. But agree about discoverability. we could add a small summary link like "2 channels suppressed (view)".

alberto: summary link helps but adds friction. greyed rows with a small suppressed badge + tooltip keeps everything visible and makes the suppression explicit at a glance. less clicks.

evelyn: from UX tests the greyed rows caused some people to miss them when scanning quickly. collapsing forces them to look at the summary, which they do notice. it's a tradeoff between scannability and discoverability.

a11y-bot: accessibility factors: collapsing removes items from the DOM unless we keep them hidden with aria. If collapsed, ensure there's an accessible disclosure with `aria-expanded` and a list of suppressed channels in the accessible tree. If greyed, do not rely on color alone; add text like "Suppressed until 4:00 PM" and ensure badges are reachable by keyboard.

marta: good point. we should treat the summary link as the canonical accessible handle for collapsed mode. copy candidates: (A) "2 channels suppressed (view)" (B) "Showing active recipients — 2 channels suppressed". which is clearer?

nina: B is more descriptive but longer. testers liked explicit phrasing in B.

sam: technical note: preview currently computes recipients from route defaults and ignores channel-level suppressions. i'll change it to compute effective recipients in order: route -> SLO overrides -> channel-level schedule. will add telemetry `preview_effective_recipients_v2`.

alberto: one more nuance: when suppressions are temporary (scheduled), users expect the preview timestamp to show when notifications resume. we should show "suppressed until 4:00 PM (local timezone)" inline in the badge/row.

a11y-bot: ensure the time string is programmatically understandable — include timezone abbreviation and consider `aria-label` like "Suppressed until 4:00 PM Pacific Daylight Time" for clarity. Also announce changes to the preview with an aria-live polite region: "Preview updated: 3 channels will receive notifications; 2 channels suppressed."

evelyn: copy for the badge tooltip: "Suppressed until 4:00 PM — this channel will not receive notifications during the window. Click to edit schedule." keeps it actionable.

marta: suggest we A/B test both patterns for 2 weeks: collapsed with summary link vs greyed rows with badges. Metrics: confusion rate in usability, clicks to find channel settings, and support tickets referencing "missing channel".

sam: will add a feature flag and telemetry to record which pattern is shown and key events (`preview_view_suppressed_clicked`, `preview_channel_edit_clicked`).

alberto: for the greyed option, ensure contrast and an explicit icon + text. for collapsed, ensure the summary link is keyboard-focusable and reveals an accessible list.

a11y-bot: final accessibility checklist to include in the spec: 1) aria-live summary updates, 2) aria-expanded on the summary disclosure, 3) keyboard-focusable badges and tooltips, 4) time string aria-labels, 5) color+icon+text for suppression state.

marta: plan: i'll add both variations to Figma and create a short lab script. nina will run 6 testers each variation. i'll share results and a final copy recommendation. thanks everyone!

evelyn: thanks - will review Figma and the copy after the first run.

sam: i'll create the feature-flag PR and wire telemetry. ping me when Figma is up.

alberto: end thread — will await test results.
